correctness.rationale: Direct symbolic differentiation reproduces both displayed density and covariance-kernel identities. Positive density for \(\alpha<0\) follows from \((1+tuv)^3\ge1\ge(1-u)(1-v)\); density for \(0\le\alpha\le1/2\) follows from a bilinear lower bound with all four corners nonnegative. The density at (0,1) excludes \(1/2<\alpha<1\), while algebraic poles exclude \(\alpha\ge1\). Uniform margins and integration give all copula axioms. For negative \(\alpha\), exact differentiation yields \(L'(t)=12(A(t)-t^2B(t))/(1+t)^2\); \(H(t)=t^2B(t)/A(t)\) has strictly positive logarithmic derivative by bounded positive expectation terms, hence exactly one root. Strictly decreasing tilt of \(q=uv\) proves \(H(2)<1\); positive-branch Spearman correlations are positive; uniform return to independence follows from an exact pointwise estimate. Reproducibility code checks identities and stable illustrative quadrature but no finite grid is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly restricts its negative parameter to preserve uniqueness of dependence values, although this restriction is not forced by two-increasingness. A full admissibility theorem and an exact unique fold tell users precisely when rank-correlation calibration ceases to identify a copula parameter, and when increasing the parameter magnitude instead returns toward independence. This is a structural model-selection/identification boundary; its value does not rest only on the modest 0.00072018 increase in attainable negative Spearman magnitude.
